$comment: Operational limits. Everything here is a judgement about cost, freshness or how long to keep something — turn it and nothing about what a fill IS changes. The constants that decide that (the fee ratio, the dust threshold, the rounding residue, the transfer topic) stay in the code beside the rule they belong to, because changing one of those changes the tape rather than the bill. Units are in the names. Served as-is at /api/limits. Also not here: network plumbing — socket heartbeats, request timeouts, reconnect backoff, page sizes bounded by the object's 128 MB — which is about whether the tape works, not about what it costs.

retention.$comment: Days. The Durable Object stops at ten gigabytes. Fills are the tape; receipts are only the evidence a rules change is replayed from, and the widest window the API serves is thirty days.

pace.$comment: Seconds between the jobs the object runs on its own clock. The books are spaced off their own last measure between booksMinSeconds and booksMaxSeconds — see booksShare. A pass stops starting new work after passBudgetSeconds and is given up on entirely after passSeconds, which is shorter than the deadline that frees the slot so two passes never overlap.

sweep.$comment: Blocks. The chain runs at about thirty blocks a second, so six thousand is roughly three minutes of it re-read, with a margin of overlap for a receipt still in flight at the last sweep's tip.

feed.$comment: DexScreener. batch is tokens quoted per pass across as many calls as that takes, stalest first; at 180 it costs 24 of the 300 calls a minute the endpoint allows. Under minLiquidityUsd a quote is not a price but the last dust that crossed an empty pool. The two ages bound how late a fill may still be given a price and a supply from a quote that arrives after it.
feed.$sweepComment: How often the quote pass looks past the fills that are actually owed a price. Those are asked for every pass, because an unpriced fill is a row the screen cannot show a dollar on; everything else is a mark that moves, and re-marking a hundred and eighty tokens four times a minute is a hundred and eighty rows written four times a minute. A row written is priced at a thousand times a row read.

migrate.$comment: Carrying the old per-row transfers onto the receipt that owns them. Bounded because the whole table at once is more memory than a Durable Object isolate has: bootRows is what opening the database may spend, so a cold object answers rather than being reset, and passRows is what one alarm may spend until the table is empty and dropped.

cache.$comment: Seconds an answer may be served from memory, by the window it covers. Never longer than the poll behind it: past that the work is already one pass per lifetime and the only thing a longer hold buys is a page slower than it looks. 'counted' is the readout, 'marked' the two pages carrying positions priced at the feed, 'edge' what the colo in front of the object holds.
cache.$totalsComment: The tape's own count, which is a walk of every fill it holds and the single most expensive thing the status line asks for. Held far longer than the poll behind it on purpose: a reader looking at a running total of forty-five thousand cannot tell it from the same number five minutes ago, and every window's own figures are counted fresh beside it.
cache.$cursorComment: A page of the tape taken behind a cursor is a page of the past: it cannot change, so it is held for as long as the reader is plausibly still paging through it. Only the first page has to be fresh, and the socket keeps that one fresher than any cache window.
cache.$stepsComment: The row counts an answer may be asked for. A limit is rounded up to the next of these before anything is read, so the edge cache cannot be walked past one row at a time: the key space is these few answers rather than every number a query string can hold. Every count the app itself asks for is on the list.
cache.$rateComment: Times one address may reach the object in a minute, counted per colo by the platform. The cache answers a reader who is behaving, so this is spent only on what the cache cannot bound: a cursor is a page of the past and every value of it is a different, entirely valid answer, so the key space behind it has no end. Configured in apps/worker/wrangler.jsonc, which is what the platform reads; the two are held together by a test.

budget.$comment: Rows a month may walk before answers start being held longer, and the most that hold may be stretched. The plan includes twenty-five billion; nothing is budgeted for overage, because the writes are what overage is for.
